title: Backup restore cannot open its staged copy when the path reaches the Windows 260-character limit
outcome: `engram backup restore` (and any SQLite open of a store-home file) works when the full path of the staged copy is 260 characters or longer on Windows, or refuses up front with a clear reason naming the path length. It never fails with a bare "unable to open database file" and a misleading remedy about installing another build.
acceptance: On Windows, backup restore succeeds when the staging file path, <home>/projects/<64-hex>/.backup-restore-<uuid>.staging, is at least 260 characters, for example by opening through an extended-length path or keeping the staging name short. If that isn't possible, it refuses before fetching with a typed reason that names the path and its length.
The restore refusal no longer suggests installing the capturing build or a migration when the real cause is an unopenable path.
A test reproduces the over-260-character staging path (deep store home) and passes.

completion.summary: Windows backup restore now handles 260/400-character staging paths through locking SQLite long-path opens, preserves logical receipts, and gives path/access errors their own recovery guidance. Full9/9 gate, independent Codex/Claude whole-input pair, fresh3/3 acceptance and all4live-store readiness passed. Six Low follow-ups filed independently.
